title: A Generalized Trace Reconstruction Problem: Recovering a String of Probabilities
authors: Joey Rivkin, Gregory Valiant, Paul Valiant
blurb: Formalizes the lower bound for the generalized trace reconstruction problem of recovering a string of probabilities from random traces.

title: A Sharp Version of Talagrand's Selector Process Conjecture and an Application to Rounding Fractional Covers
blurb: Formalizes a sharp version of Talagrand's selector process conjecture and its consequence for rounding fractional covers to integral ones.

title: Approximation Guarantees of the Median Mechanism in ℝᵈ
blurb: Formalizes the dimension-independent approximation ratio of the coordinate-wise median mechanism in ℝᵈ.

title: Efficiently Learning Mixtures of Two Gaussians
authors: Adam Tauman Kalai, Ankur Moitra, Gregory Valiant
blurb: Formalizes that the first six moments of a one-dimensional mixture of two Gaussians suffice to robustly recover its parameters.

title: Refuting the Direct Sum Conjecture for Total Functions in Deterministic Communication Complexity
blurb: Formalizes a counterexample refuting the direct sum conjecture for total functions in deterministic communication complexity.

title: A Proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture
blurb: Formalizes a proof of the cycle double cover conjecture — every finite bridgeless graph has a collection of cycles covering each edge exactly twice — reducing it to an elementary linear-algebra argument over 𝔽₂³.

title: Planar Point Sets with Many Unit Distances
blurb: Formalizes the disproof of Erdős's unit-distance conjecture: an infinite unramified 3-tower of totally real fields yields n-point planar sets with ν(n) ≥ n^{1+δ} unit distances for infinitely many n.

title: The Strong Perfect Graph Theorem
authors: Maria Chudnovsky, Neil Robertson, Paul Seymour, Robin Thomas
blurb: Formalizes the strong perfect graph theorem — a graph is perfect if and only if it is Berge — through the paper's structure theorem: every Berge graph is basic, or one of it and its complement admits a proper 2-join, or it admits a proper homogeneous pair or a balanced skew partition. The main theorem is sorry-free with only Lean's three foundational axioms.

title: Graph Isomorphism in Quasipolynomial Time
blurb: Formalizes Babai's quasipolynomial-time algorithm for Graph Isomorphism and String Isomorphism — including the Design Lemma, Split-or-Johnson, the Main Structure Theorem for alternating quotients, Local Certificates, and the Master Algorithm on an explicit random access machine, together with an explicit running-time bound of exp(O((log N)⁵)). The formalization is sorry-free and rests only on five cited group-theoretic theorems.
